summary: AI observability has become essential in 2026 as LLM-powered applications move into production, with New Relic reporting 30% quarter-over-quarter growth in AI monitoring adoption. These tools capture the full trace behind production outcomes—prompts, responses, retrieval context, tool calls, and costs—helping teams detect hallucinations, model drift, and runaway spending. Observability goes beyond traditional APM by explaining *why* model signals changed, not just *that* they changed.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: End-to-end LLM application traces across the full agent workflow including LLM calls, retrieval, tool execution, prompts, and token/cost usage.
features: Detailed tracing and monitoring charts for LLM-specific stats
Deep native integration with the LangChain ecosystem
Comprehensive cost visibility across the full agent workflow
tools.pricing: Consumption/trace-based. Roughly $264 for 100,000 traces at high-volume deployments; overage charges can run ~5–10% of underlying LLM API spend for trace-heavy workloads. Free developer tier available.
tools.best_for: Teams already building on LangChain/LangGraph that want deep, comprehensive observability across complex agent workflows.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API request/response logging, token usage, latency, and cost governance via a lightweight proxy.
features: One-line base URL change for setup (lightweight proxy)
Cost governance implementable in under five minutes
Caching and rate-limiting for cost control
tools.pricing: Usage-priced with a generous free tier. Helicone Pro reaches 100,000 traces at ~$79 — significantly cheaper than LangSmith for the same volume.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting instant, low-friction cost visibility and governance across providers without framework lock-in.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B Weave)
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, experiment tracking, model evaluations, and ML/LLM lifecycle metrics.
features: W&B Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
tools.pricing: Free tier for individuals; team and enterprise plans are subscription-based with usage components (custom enterprise pricing).
tools.best_for: ML/AI teams that want unified experiment tracking and LLM observability across the full model development lifecycle.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Production LLM/ML performance, model drift, embedding/data quality, and evaluation traces.
features: Open-source Arize Phoenix with OpenTelemetry integration
Embedding analysis and data quality monitoring
tools.pricing: Phoenix is open-source and free to self-host; Arize AX offers free and paid enterprise tiers with consumption-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams needing rigorous, standards-based (OpenTelemetry) evaluation and drift detection for production ML and LLM systems.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompts, token usage, costs, and evaluation scores — fully self-hostable.
tools.pricing: Self-host is free (compute + storage costs only), making it the cheapest option for high volumes. Managed cloud offers free, pro, and enterprise tiers.
tools.best_for: Cost-conscious teams wanting a full-featured, open-source observability stack with the option to self-host for data control.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, and metrics exported via OpenTelemetry standards to any compatible backend.
features: Vendor-neutral — export to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, etc.
Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and vector DBs
tools.pricing: Free and open-source (SDK/instrumentation layer); you pay only for whatever backend you export telemetry to.
tools.best_for: Teams that want standards-based, vendor-neutral LLM telemetry feeding into their existing observability backend.

cost_tips: Use a proxy-based tool (like Helicone) to enable prompt caching and semantic caching, so repeated or similar queries don't re-hit the model and incur full API costs.
Route requests to the smallest capable model and reserve expensive frontier models for complex tasks; implement model tiering and fallback logic via a gateway (e.g., Portkey).
Set per-user, per-department, and per-project budget alerts and rate limits to catch runaway spend early—observability without cost governance leaves you blind to overage charges.
Trim prompt and context size by pruning retrieval chunks, compressing system prompts, and limiting max output tokens, since token count directly drives cost in consumption-based pricing.
Consider self-hosting an open-source observability stack (Langfuse or Arize Phoenix) for high-volume workloads where per-trace SaaS fees can reach 5–10% of your underlying LLM spend.
